$sources: BSL Enforcement Order Art. 82(2) table: the long-term and short-term stresses by the combination of G (fixed load), P (live load), S (snow), W (wind) and K (seismic force), ordinary and heavy-snow areas
BSL Enforcement Order Art. 82(2) note: where uplift or overturning is checked, P by the actual state (taken as 0)
source: BSL Enforcement Order Art. 82: the allowable stress combinations (the members' primary design checks them against the long-term and the short-term allowable stresses, allowableStress.longTerm naming the long-term rows): long-term G + P (ordinary areas), G + P + 0.7S (heavy-snow areas); short-term G + P + S, G + P + W (and G + P + 0.35S + W in heavy-snow areas), G + P + K (G + P + 0.35S + K). D stands for G, L and Lr for P, E for K. The heavy-snow rows are formed wherever the project has a snow case S (in an ordinary area they are on the safe side). The strength combinations are SAEngine practice for sizing the bars with the parent's strength method (not the law's): the long-term rows × 1.5 (about F / ft of the long-term allowable bar stress), the short-term rows × 1.0 (ft = F).
